note: CLEAN PASS WITH CAVEATS (batch_321, 2026-09-23). 75 rows = 15 items x 5 levels; validate_items.R --table-sets passes both sets (15/15 items, resp 1-5). CODE DERIVATION: data/sabers_vesper2023.R reads me_N1361.sav and takes the 15 columns by name (nms vector), so each IRW code IS the source column name (pattern 1, no rename, no positional step). MAPPING data_labels: 11 columns (leg1, leg2, info1-3, sozn1-3, unt1-3) carry their English item wording as their own variable label in me_N1361.sav, identical to the raw file English labels, 11/11. The 4 reversed columns negaf1_r, negaf2_r, negaf3_r, leg3_r are labelled only e.g. "negaf1 recoded"; Syntax.sps ties each to its source (RECODE negaf1 (1=5) (2=4) (3=3) (4=2) (5=1) INTO negaf1_r), and negaf1/negaf2/negaf3/leg3 carry the labels I feel disturbed by strikes. / Strikes strain myself. / I am annoyed by strikes. / Strikes are a waste of time. The code names are also self-describing by factor (negaf=negative reactions, leg=legitimacy, info=informing oneself, sozn=social network behaviour, unt=support), consistent with the items PDF grouping 15/15. Step 5b exempt (pattern 1 + level-1 labels); no verification row written. REVERSED ANCHORS (resp axis): the live _r items are stored reverse-scored, so option_text runs Agree(1)..Do not agree(5) for those four items. Checked: in me_N1361.sav the negaf1 x negaf1_r crosstab is exactly 6-x (1->5 n=307, 2->4 220, 3->3 382, 4->2 299, 5->1 153; same pattern for negaf2, negaf3, leg3), and the live table matches the reversed column, not the raw one: item_stats.R floor/ceiling for negaf1_r 11.2%/22.6% = 153/1361 and 307/1361; leg3_r floor 8.2% = 111/1361 (raw leg3=5 count). OPTIONS: English value labels on every item in both .sav files: 1 Do not agree, 2 Partially disagree, 3 Neither disagree, nor agree, 4 Partially agree, 5 Agree (items PDF note confirms endpoints 1 = Do not agree ... 5 = Agree). WORDING: item_text is the raw survey export English labels verbatim except one export artifact: unt3 reads strikers^ position in both .sav files and was shipped as strikers’ position, the form the items PDF prints. Beyond unt3, the items PDF differs from the survey export in two places, and the export (what the survey software held) was preferred: sozn1 PDF on the social media vs export in the social media; sozn2 PDF I comment on posts about strikes on the social media vs export I comment posts about strikes in the social media; the other 12 items are identical in both. INSTRUCTIONS blank: no question stem or instruction text in the deposit (neither .sav, the syntax, the preregistrations nor the items PDF); the paper full text could not be fetched (Cloudflare challenge on econtent.hogrefe.com), so instructions may exist there. LANGUAGE: three-version administration, language variable English 444 / Deutsch 454 / Francais 463 in me_N1361.sav. English base fields, no _translated columns, language = English; German; French (order of the paper title), per the szameitat_2015_* ruling. The German and French wording (item labels and anchors, e.g. Stimme nicht zu..Stimme zu; Pas daccord..Daccord) IS published in the deposit (raw .sav labels v_168..v_182 and v_105..v_119, and the items PDF) but the one-text-per-item schema cannot carry three versions. STEP 3b: matches - 15 items, 5 factors x 3, 1-5 agreement scale, the SABeRS as listed in the items PDF; the table excludes the willingness-to-strike (sb*) and system-justification (sj*) items in the same file. RIGHTS: SABeRS is the authors own scale (Vesper and Koenig); the items PDF is deposited by them on OSF under CC BY 4.0, and the article is CC BY; instrument_rights_register.csv has no SABeRS/strike-attitude row; no fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution clause located. note: Code derivation: data/cnes.R melts sem::CNES with item = names(x)[i], so the IRW item code IS the source column name (pattern 1, no positional step), and resp = match(label, c(StronglyDisagree, Disagree, Agree, StronglyAgree)). An .rda has no variable labels, so the tie from code to wording is the package documentation: CNES.Rd states each statement against its exact column name (paper_explicit). The ICPSR 2593 codebook independently labels the same CES 1997 mail-back variables MBSA2 Be More Tolerant People Choose Standards, MBSA7 NewerLifestyles Contrib BreakdownSociety, MBSA8 Change=Adapt Our View Of Moral Behaviour, MBSA9 Fewer Problems=Traditional Family Values (4/4 consistent). item_text is the CNES.Rd statement verbatim (dQuote marks dropped). DEVIATION, disclosed: option_text renders the R factor levels StronglyDisagree/Disagree/Agree/StronglyAgree with spaces and sentence case (Strongly disagree ... Strongly agree); the printed questionnaire card wording was not located (the CES 1997 questionnaires are distributed separately from the technical documentation and were not retrievable; the ICPSR codebook is a variable list only), so the exact anchor wording respondents read is unconfirmed. instructions and section_prompt blank: no questionnaire text for the battery lead-in was available. LANGUAGE: the CES 1997 was fielded in English and French (tech doc: Both the English and French interviewing...; codebook variable MBSQLANG Language Of Questionnaire), so language = English; French; the base fields hold the English version, the only one in the deposit (sem package); the French wording is not in the deposit or Fox (2006) and was not shipped. Step 3b: live table is exactly these 4 items, resp 1-4, 1529 ids, matching the CNES.Rd description of four 4-level traditional-values items; no mismatch. Verification (verify_sem_cnes.R): all 16 item x level counts match the CRAN .rda cell for cell (e.g. MBSA9 75/327/626/501), and polarity is as the wording predicts (r(MBSA7,MBSA9)=+0.47, r(MBSA2,MBSA8)=+0.24, all four cross pairs -0.19..-0.30). RIGHTS: wording copied from the GPL (>= 2) sem package documentation; CES 1997 is an academic election study (York ISR / Blais, Gidengil, Nadeau, Nevitte) distributed through ICPSR; no fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause on the question wording was located. Silence treated as permission; no register row written.
public_note: The 1997 Canadian Election Study mail-back questionnaire was administered in English or French; this table carries the English statements only, as documented in the R sem package, and the response labels are rendered from that package's factor levels (Strongly disagree to Strongly agree) rather than transcribed from the printed questionnaire
